_comment: REQUIRED BY DEFAULT. A registered type binds on EVERY action unless an entry says otherwise, and saying otherwise costs a stated `reason`. The minimal entry {"family": "..."} is the STRICT one -- adding a type is one line and it binds immediately. Inclusion is free; exclusion is the thing that takes effort.
_why: The first draft listed required steps explicitly per action, so adding a checker meant writing it AND remembering to add it to the list. Forget the second half and the checker runs, passes, and counts for nothing -- absence rendering as success, in the very file that defines what complete means. A registry you must remember to extend is a registry that will be incomplete.
_reasonless_narrowing: An `actions` or `when` narrowing with NO `reason` is IGNORED and the type falls back to required-for-all. This is the encoding_whitelist.txt convention, reused deliberately because it is already familiar here: nothing is suppressed until a human has actually looked. A typo in an exemption fails safe.
_unregistered: V8 rejects a record whose step is not listed here, record.py returns None, and the checker exits 2 -- so the pipeline blocks the moment someone wires in an unregistered check, loudly, at the desk of the person who can fix it. That is the pair that closes the hole: you cannot add a check that silently does not count, and you cannot register one that silently is not required.

copy_editor.reason: the D9 copy-editor panel: THREE agents read the adversary-passed state, editorial's branch and the published prior-art references, independently, and judge whether the MEANING survived editorial's prose changes. Findings UNION across all three so a lone reader who catches a meaning shift is never outvoted; only the VERDICT is voted, 2-of-3. A split records UNDECIDED and escalates. Brief: `.claude/commands/copy-editor.md`. ⚠ `failing` is admitted on UNDECIDED precisely for this: a 2-1 split over forty files is undecided about the ONE line they disagree on and decided about the other thirty-nine, so the dispute is recorded NARROW rather than indicting the scope. ⭐ WHAT IT GATES, AND WHY ONLY THERE: `tag` alone -- the published prose surface at the moment a RELEASE is cut. This is the last gate in the chain, running after adversary, editorial and prior-art, and the only one whose readers' briefs carry the `R-BEDROCK` invariants, so it is the one check positioned to catch a meaning shift that the prose gates introduced rather than found. A release mints a permanent Zenodo DOI and a flaw inside a published PDF cannot be withdrawn; a commit is a rollback point and a push is not yet publication, so spending three reader-agents there would price every arc -- including arcs touching no core object -- for a risk only the release carries. It is scoped to the paths `editorial` can change, because a copy-editor panel can only ever be about a change editorial was able to make, and it discharges that scope FILE BY FILE: a path cleared stays cleared until its bytes move, and a path never examined stays OWED rather than silent.

_switches_v15: A subject set is everything the verdict DEPENDS ON, not merely everything the checker read. Found by ZeroParadox 2026-08-23: check_pov recorded 291 subjects and NOT pov_baseline.txt, so grandfathering a violation into that baseline left the record reading SATISFIED -- every file it named was unchanged. V15 refuses a record that omits a declared switch, which turns a convention into a contract: with the switch as a subject, editing a baseline moves a blob the record names, the key goes STALE, and the checker re-runs. Declaring switches is NOT a narrowing and costs no reason -- it makes a type stricter.

Found by ZeroParadox's /rely trial: a planted DENIAL made check_pov exit 1, one appended allowlist line made it exit 0, AND NO SUBJECT MOVED. _approved_modules: ⛔⛔ WHICH BUILD MAY RECORD, not merely which file. `module` pins the PATH, so an EDITED checker records exactly as readily as a reviewed one. `approved_modules` lists the blob ids this step accepts, and verdictLedger's V16c REFUSES a record whose `evidence` names an unapproved build. Pinned for PUSH-GATING steps ONLY -- advisory and commit-only steps stay unpinned, so the friction is paid where publication is decided and nowhere else. ⛔⛔ WHEN A CHECKER GETS A NEW BUILD, **REPLACE** THE HASH -- DO NOT ADD TO THE LIST. `["<new>"]` is correct; `["<old>", "<new>"]` is wrong absent a stated expiry. ⚠⚠ AN ACCUMULATING LIST STOPS BEING A PIN: approve v1, v2, v3, v4 and eventually every build ever written is approved -- still LOOKING pinned while constraining nothing. That is `RLY31-6`'s exact shape, where a control decayed into permissiveness while appearing to hold and nothing was positioned to notice; this is the same trap in a different field. The history is already versioned, so every past approved set is recoverable from this file's own log -- a list inside the field duplicates that, and the duplicate is the copy that rots. Old records need no entry either: nothing re-validates the stored stream (`validate` runs only at append), so a record made under v1 stays exactly as valid as the day it landed. THE ONLY LEGITIMATE PAIR IS A ROLLOUT WINDOW -- v2 shipping while a run is in flight on v1 -- and it needs a STATED EXPIRY the way `copy_editor`'s `_why_not_admitted_yet` does, or the transitional pair quietly becomes permanent. ⭐ THE TWO-STEP COST IS SMALLER THAN IT LOOKS, and this was measured in the server's `inventory.py` rather than assumed: EDITING A CHECKER ALREADY STALES EVERY ROW IT PRODUCED, pinned or not -- `ev_stale` compares each record's `evidence` against current content and reports that the producer changed. So a new build means re-running that step regardless of `approved_modules`, and approving the new blob is ONE LINE IN THE SAME COMMIT THAT SHIPS THE CODE, inside a re-run you already owe. Tim's ruling on the trade: "the 'silently can't record' is the problem. fail loudly." V16c refuses naming BOTH the rejected blob and this field, and approving is a REVIEWABLE EDIT in the same history as the tool change -- the point of pinning rather than an obstacle to it. ⚠ A step with NO `approved_modules` still records; `policy()` reports `unpinned_modules`, so an unpinned step is DISCLOSED rather than silently permitted. ⚠⚠ EVERY BLOB BELOW WAS RE-DERIVED IN THIS TREE with `record.module_evidence`, the same function that computes evidence at record time, and NOT pasted from the message that proposed them. Pinning a stale blob refuses the very next run of that checker, so a copied list is the one thing this field must never contain. ⚠ THE STEP NAME IS NOT THE FILE NAME: `claim_review` pins `check_frozen.py` and `decls` pins `batch.py`. This entry's own `module` is the authority for that mapping. ⚠ IF YOU ADD A REGISTRY KEY AND IT SEEMS IGNORED: the server's `Config.requirements()` rebuilds each spec key by key from a whitelist rather than passing the entry through, so a key absent from that whitelist is invisible to every rule downstream no matter what this file says.
